newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq drops at opening, Intel leads tech decline.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq drops at opening, Intel leads tech decline.

text.p: The Nasdaq composite index dropped 47.24 points to 1355.80 at the opening bell Friday, with bellwether Intel Corp off 20-49/64 to 143.
Intel said early today that its second quarter results would fall short of its expectations.
Most major technology stocks lost ground.
Overall, Declining issues led gainers by nearly four to one, with 1,856 losers compared to 459 gainers, on volume of 60 million shares as of 0943 EDT/1343 GMT.
Dell Computer Corp fell 8-1/8 to 102-1/8, Microsoft Corp dropped 6-3/4 to 199-1/8, and Cisco Systems Inc slid 4-1/4 to 62-5/8.
The Philadelphia Stock Exchange semiconductor index lost 15.27 points, or 4.79 percent, to 303.77.
Of the 25 most active Nasdaq issues, only one stock, Cyrix Corp, showed gains, up one point to 23-1/8.
The drop in technology stocks touched nearly every sector, from semiconductor stocks to personal computer makers to networking companies, traders said.

"Could it (the Nasdaq) go lower? Sure it could," said Nicholas Karos, senior over-the-counter trader at Piper Jaffray. "But it's already dropped a lot. It all depends on where the techs wash out today.
"For Intel, this is the first hiccup they've had in recent memory. Has the psychology changed on Intel? I don't know."
The American Stock Exchange Internet Index lost 7.69 points, or 3.13 percent, to 238.15. The Morgan Stanley High Tech Index shed 13.68 points, or 3.18 percent, to 416.13.
The selloff hit the largest names the hardest, traders said. Small-capitalization stocks were mostly spared as the focus remained on the large-cap technology sector leaders, they said.
The Russell 2000 index, a key barometer of small-cap stocks, lost only 3.58 points, or 0.95 percent, to 374.85.
Some traders said some high-tech stocks might recover slightly by the end of the day.
"There's people out there waiting to put cash to work. They may be waiting to buy after some of the dust settles," said Brett Discher, vice president of equity trading at Dain Bosworth.
Nasdaq shares had recovered slightly by 1016 EDT/1416 GMT. The Nasdaq composite index was off 33.89 points at 1369.15.
